thread:
alex.k: Heads-up — proposing a Dedicated slice deploy for PolarisCare tonight 02:00-03:30 UTC. Requesting approvals and confirmation on rollback thresholds + version pinning.

deploy-bot: [auto] Scheduled deployment job created
  - customer: PolarisCare (dedicated slice)
  - target image: redwood-inference:v3.2.1-rc4
  - fallback image: redwood-inference:v3.1.9
  - canary: 10% traffic for 20m -> roll to 100% if healthy
  - change window: 2026-03-21 02:00:00 -> 2026-03-21 03:30:00 UTC
  - runbook: /runbooks/polariscare-dedicated-deploy.md

priya.s: +1 on the window for product. PolarisCare requested off-peak, this fits.

kevin.l: FYI CS reached out — customer has one batch job at 03:00 UTC but they said it can be postponed by 45m. They gave provisional OK if we stick to canary and keep latency SLAs.

jenna.sre: Quick questions:
  - What are the rollback criteria?
  - Which metrics will trigger immediate rollback vs. slow ramp?

alex.k: Proposal: rollback if error_rate increases by >3% absolute OR 95th latency delta >200ms sustained for 5m. Immediate rollback for 5xx spike >1% absolute or tail latency >500ms. Also abort if redis cache miss rate doubles.

jenna.sre: Sounds reasonable. Add a soft-fallback route to v3.1.9 for critical requests (pin by customer ID) before full rollback so we can minimize churn.

deploy-bot: note: runtime-config: batching=auto, kv-cache=on, quantize=fp16 (no int8)

priya.s: Product approves with the pinning plan. Priya S. +approve :white_check_mark:

kevin.l: CS approves as long as we notify PolarisCare 30m before canary start. I'll send the notice at T-30.

ops-oncall: Oncall confirms availability between 01:30-04:00 UTC. I'll be the pager and will watch traces.

alex.k: Rollout plan summary:
  1) 02:00 — start canary (10%) for 20m, monitoring dashboard + smoke tests
  2) 02:20 — if green, ramp to 50% for 10m, run canary eval set
  3) 02:30 — ramp to 100% if still green, hold 30m for post-checks
  4) 03:00 — run scheduled customer batch check; if that fails, soft-route to fallback
  5) 03:30 — end window; if any open issues, keep slice pinned to v3.1.9 and open incident

jenna.sre: Add these dashboards to the alert group:
  - /dash/polariscare/latency
  - /dash/polariscare/errors
  - /dash/polariscare/p95-p99
  - alert: polaris_5xx_rate > 1% for 3m -> SEV2
  - alert: polaris_p95_delta > 200ms for 5m -> paged

alex.k: I'll attach the release notes in the runbook (model/kernel changes, kernel selection logic, batching tweaks).

deploy-bot: checklist status:
  - canary config: set
  - traffic routing rules: staged
  - customer notify: pending (kevin.l)
  - regression tests: passed (smoke + embed sanity)

kevin.l: Notifying customer now. msg: "PolarisCare — planned Dedicated slice update starting in 30 minutes. We'll run a 10% canary and will notify on any regressions. Reply if concerns."

priya.s: minor ask: pin model version in per-slice config so customer can opt-out of auto-roll for 24h after deploy.

alex.k: done — set slice.pin_hold = 24h post-deploy. Also enabling automatic fallback policy to v3.1.9 if immediate rollback triggers.

jenna.sre: Approved from SRE side. I'll be monitoring and ready to execute rollback if thresholds hit.

ops-oncall: +1. Oncall will execute soft-route if needed, then full rollback if not resolved in 10m.

deploy-bot: [auto] Deployment job will proceed at scheduled time. Escalation channel: #eng-oncall -> @ops-oncall.

alex.k: Thanks all — proceeding with the plan. If anyone needs to opt-out now speak up.

kevin.l: Customer acknowledged and is standing by.

priya.s: Approved from product and PM. Good to go. :rocket:

jenna.sre: Postmortem note: capture the canary telemetry and customer batch run results in the incident log regardless of success.

alex.k: Will file a short release note after the window with observed metrics and any deviations.

ops-oncall: I'll close the loop once the slice either stays on v3.2.1-rc4 or we roll back.

deploy-bot: [auto] Final status: scheduled -> queued (T-120m)

alex.k: thread locked for changes after 01:45 UTC unless urgent.

kevin.l: Thanks everyone."
